post.a: One published item on one channel. A LinkedIn post and a blog article from the same idea are two.

approve.q: Can I approve before it publishes?
approve.a: Yes — turn Autopilot off and everything stays in the pipeline for you to review. Or leave it on and let the quality gate be the reviewer.

down.q: What if the AI is down?
down.a: The post waits. Contivo never publishes something the gate could not review.

pricing.closeHeadline: Nothing to decide yet. It is <accent>free</accent> while we prove it.

meta.title: Content API — Contivo for developers
meta.description: Read your published Contivo posts from any stack with one authenticated GET. Endpoints, parameters, response shape, errors, caching and the revalidate webhook.

siteApi.title: Content API
siteApi.lede: Your site reads its published posts from Contivo with one authenticated GET. Nothing is pushed into your codebase, there is no plugin, and it works with any stack that can make an HTTP request.

howItWorks.p1: Contivo writes and publishes on the schedule you set. When a post goes live it is assigned a permanent slug and marked published — and that is the end of Contivo's involvement. Your site asks for posts when it wants them.
howItWorks.p2: That direction matters: Contivo never has write access to your codebase, your deploy pipeline or your CMS. If you turn Contivo off, your site keeps serving whatever it last fetched.

auth.p1: Every request carries a site key as a bearer token. Create one under <link>Connections → Websites</link>. It is shown once, at creation, and cannot be recovered afterwards — if you lose it, create a new site connection.
auth.p2: Keep the key server-side. It can read everything this workspace has ever published. The endpoints do send permissive CORS headers, so a browser can call them — but doing so ships your key to every visitor. Fetch in a server component, a route handler, at build time, or from your backend.

list.p1: Returns published posts for the workspace that owns the key, newest first.
list.limit: How many posts to return. Values outside the range are clamped, not rejected.
list.cursor: The nextCursor from a previous response. Omit for the first page.
list.channel: Which channel to return. Pass "all" to include social posts too — usually you do not want these on a website.
list.p2: nextCursor is null when there are no more pages. That is the only reliable end-of-list signal — do not stop on a short page.

single.p1: Returns post with the same object as above. Route your pages on slug, never on id: the slug is assigned once at publish and never changes, which is what keeps your URLs stable.

postObject.id: Stable internal identifier. Good as a React key, not for URLs.
postObject.slug: URL-safe, unique per workspace, permanent from the moment of publish.
postObject.title: The post topic.
postObject.content: The full body, as Markdown. Render it with whatever you already use.
postObject.excerpt: First ~200 characters with Markdown stripped. For cards, lists and meta descriptions.
postObject.channel: Normally "blog". Only other values if you asked for channel=all.
postObject.updatedAt: ISO 8601 UTC. Useful for cache keys, sitemaps and lastmod.

errors.unauthorized: Missing, malformed, unknown or revoked key — or the site connection is not active. All four return the same response on purpose, so nobody can use this endpoint to work out which keys exist.
errors.notFound: Single post only. No published post with that slug in this workspace. A slug belonging to another customer also returns 404, never 403.
errors.p1: An empty posts array is not an error. It means the key is valid and nothing has been published to that channel yet — Autopilot has to publish something before anything appears here.

caching.p1: Responses are sent with Cache-Control: no-store, so the API never asks a CDN or browser to hold onto them. Caching is entirely yours to decide, which is the right way round: your framework knows your traffic and your tolerance for staleness.
caching.p2: A five-minute window is a sensible default. For instant updates, pair a long revalidate with the webhook below rather than polling harder.

revalidate.p1: Optional. Set a revalidate URL on the site connection and Contivo will call it right after each publish, so your cache clears immediately instead of on the next interval.
revalidate.p2: The call times out after 8 seconds and its status is recorded against the site connection. A failure is logged and never blocks the publish — the post is already live and your site will pick it up on its next scheduled fetch regardless.

recipes.paging: Fetch every post, one page at a time

limits.methodsNotes: Read-only. There is no way to write content through this API.
limits.pageSizeNotes: Larger values are clamped rather than rejected.
limits.scopeNotes: A key can only ever read the workspace it was created in.
limits.slugsNotes: Assigned at publish, never rewritten. Safe to use in URLs and sitemaps.
limits.revokingNotes: Deleting or disabling a site connection makes its key 401 on the next request.
limits.p1: There is no published rate limit today. Cache your responses anyway — a site that fetches on every page view is fragile for its own reasons, not just ours.

siteApi.footerNote: Something here wrong or missing? It is generated from the same code that serves the API, so a mismatch is a bug worth reporting. Print this page to save it as a PDF.

guide.toggleTitle: How to use your site key
guide.toggleBody: Your site reads posts from Contivo. Nothing is pushed into your codebase, and there is no plugin to install.
guide.step1Title: 1 · Store the key as an env var
guide.step1Body: It is shown once, when you create it. Put it in your hosting provider's environment as CONTIVO_SITE_KEY and never in client-side code — the key reads everything this workspace has published. Lost it? Create a new site connection; keys cannot be recovered.
guide.step3Body: Any framework works: it is one authenticated GET returning JSON. Call it server-side so the key never reaches the browser.

fields.id: Stable identifier. Use it as a React key, not in your URLs.
fields.slug: URL-safe, assigned at publish and never changed afterwards. Route on this.
fields.title: The post topic.
fields.excerpt: First ~200 characters, already stripped of Markdown. For cards and meta descriptions.
fields.channel: Always "blog" unless you asked for others.
fields.publishedAt: ISO 8601, or null if not published.
fields.updatedAt: ISO 8601. Useful for cache keys and sitemaps.

guide.trouble401: <c>401</c> — the key is wrong, revoked, or the site connection is not active. Check the status above.
guide.trouble404: <c>404</c> on a single post — that slug is not published. Slugs are assigned at publish time, not when a draft is written.
guide.troubleEmpty: <c>posts: []</c> — the key is fine, nothing is published to the blog channel yet. Autopilot has to publish before anything appears here.
guide.revalidateNote: Optional: set a revalidate URL on the site connection and Contivo will ping it after each publish, so your cache refreshes immediately instead of on the next interval.
